A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDE tokenizer and MUSE-VL research work. All pages, equations, tables, figures and references support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original multimodal understanding results, image-reconstruction measurements, LLM/resolution ablations and qualitative generation and VQA examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original understanding and reconstruction experiments and adds quantitative image-generation results in Table 5 and tokenizer-branch ablations in Table 6.

M1.justification: Both versions use frozen SigLIP semantic features, feature fusion and vector quantization, semantic and image decoders, the same combined losses, and autoregressive modeling with an expanded LLM vocabulary. The new branch ablation tests existing components. Expanded decoder descriptions and redrawn diagrams do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v3 adds MJHQ-30K and GenEval evaluation, substantially expanding quantitative coverage of image generation. MME evaluation and the Chinese MMBench tokenizer results disappear. The pretraining description also narrows from image/video pairs, interleaved documents and text-only data to image-caption pairs; this establishes changed reported coverage, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E2.justification: Janus joins the understanding comparison in Table 1, while VILA-U and RQ-VAE join reconstruction Table 3. New generation Table 5 includes comparators such as SDv1.5, PixArt, SD-XL, Playground v2.5, DALL-E3, SEED-X and LWM. Earlier qualitative comparisons against SEED-LLaMA, LaVIT, Emu2 and Chameleon are removed from their respective case studies.

E3.justification: New protocols include FID between 30K generated and 30K reference images, GenEval with and without prompt rewriting, and image-only, semantic-only and joint branch controls. Existing summaries also change metric composition: Table 2 excludes Chinese MMBench, and the scaling ablation drops AI2D and adds an average. The ImageNet 50K reconstruction protocol at 256 × 256 remains.

E4.justification: New Table 6 directly tests the separate and combined contributions of semantic and image branches to understanding and reconstruction. Table 4 adds a training-data-volume comparison. The LLM/resolution ablation is retained as Table 7, but v1's reconstruction, comparative text-to-image and VQA error case studies are removed. The semantic-code visualization is largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added benchmark averages and generation metrics do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises reported 7B results, including MMStar 48.3 to 49.6 and MMMU 42.3 to 39.7; SEED-LLaMA's MMBench entry changes from 45.8 to 28.7. Retained 32B benchmark scores are unchanged. New results include MJHQ-30K FID 7.73, GenEval 0.53/0.57 with rewriting, and branch-ablation outcomes. These are reported revisions and additions, not established same-setting gains; several changed averages also use different metric sets.

T1.justification: The quantization construction and semantic, reconstruction and VQ loss equations remain equivalent. Clarifying code indices versus embeddings and replacing z-prime with z-q are notational refinements. Neither version contains substantive theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain semantic-aware tokenization and unified autoregressive understanding and generation. v3 explicitly claims superiority on generation benchmarks and presents SDE as avoiding VILA-U's loss conflicts. Its abstract also makes the retained understanding-superiority claim more specific through quantified Emu3 and LLaVA-NeXT comparisons.

C2.justification: v3 adds an argument that reconstructing pretrained semantic features avoids contrastive/reconstruction loss conflicts, interprets the branch controls as separating understanding from reconstructability, and attributes reduced data requirements to easier alignment. It also discusses reconstruction versus code-size tradeoffs with VILA-U. Earlier case-based interpretations concerning reconstruction errors, prompt omissions and VQA hallucinations are removed.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly identifies ImageNet-1K, CC12M, Cambrian7M and LLaVA-OneVision sources by training stage and specifies a BEITv2-style semantic decoder. Table 1 adds base-LLM and resolution information. Core tokenizer and optimizer hyperparameters remain unchanged, while v1's instruction to preserve aspect ratio during generation-image resizing is omitted. These are principally documentation changes.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially reposition SDE against Emu3's separately fine-tuned models, Janus's separate encoders, TokenFlow's dual codebooks and VILA-U's contrastive alignment. v3 adds a visual-tokenization survey covering residual and multiscale quantization, discusses Transfusion, and adds references supporting the expanded generation comparisons and training-data disclosures.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around semantic information loss and comparisons with recent unified models. Related work gains a dedicated visual-tokenization subsection. Experiments are reorganized with explicit evaluation setup, visual generation and ablation discussions, while qualitative evaluation is substantially condensed.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 are redrawn; Figure 1 changes its radar-chart coverage and image gallery. Earlier reconstruction, generation-comparison and VQA panels are removed or replaced by a new generation gallery, and Figure 5 is condensed. Tables gain new grouping, LLM/resolution columns and revised metric/code-size columns, alongside new training-volume, generation and branch-ablation tables.

improvement.justification: v1 supported generation mainly with selected examples and did not directly isolate both tokenizer branches. v3's quantitative generation benchmarks and branch ablation address these central evidentiary gaps, substantially strengthening support for unified understanding and generation. Training-source disclosures also improve reproducibility. The removed qualitative comparisons and an abstract generation-superiority claim broader than Table 5's mixed results temper, but do not outweigh, these gains.
